analyses.name: Apple Inc.
analyses.verdict: The only mega-cap tech name that closed at relative-strength highs while the rest of large-cap tech broke — but earnings in 2 days at a 35x forward multiple means new money waits for the print.

financials.summary: Apple's last full fiscal year was a reacceleration year rather than a maintenance year. The iPhone franchise returned to unit and revenue growth after a soft prior cycle, and Services — the App Store, iCloud, advertising, payments and subscription bundles — continued compounding at a materially faster rate than hardware, which is what actually drives the margin story. Because Services carries far higher gross margin than devices, the mix shift lifted consolidated gross margin even in quarters where hardware pricing was competitive. The balance sheet remains the defining feature: an enormous net cash position, a very large annual free-cash-flow number, and a buyback programme big enough that share count shrinks meaningfully every year, so EPS grows faster than net income by construction. The current scan captures the result — revenue +16.6% and EPS +21.8% year over year, the EPS line running ahead of revenue exactly as the buyback-plus-mix mechanism predicts.
highlights: Revenue +16.6% YoY — a clear reacceleration from the prior cycle's flat-to-down comparisons
EPS +21.8% YoY, outpacing revenue growth on Services mix plus buyback-driven share-count reduction
Services remains the fastest-growing and highest-margin segment, and is now the primary driver of consolidated gross margin expansion
Installed base of active devices at record levels, which is the leading indicator for Services revenue
Free cash flow generation and net cash position remain best-in-class among mega-caps, funding one of the largest buyback programmes in the market
Forward P/E of 35.0 — a premium to Apple's own historical range, so the multiple now embeds the reacceleration

accomplishments: Re-established iPhone growth after a multi-quarter plateau, proving the upgrade cycle was deferred rather than lost
Grew Services to the point where it, not hardware, sets the direction of consolidated gross margin
Executed on-device AI features across the installed base without the capex burden that has hit the hyperscalers — Apple is monetising AI at the edge rather than funding data centres
Sustained a buyback large enough to shrink share count materially, adding several points of EPS growth annually
Grew the active-device installed base to a new record, widening the annuity base under Services

journey_52w.summary: A year of steady re-rating that ended with Apple as the last mega-cap standing. Apple climbed to 338.19 at this session's close, just 0.6% below its 52-week high, holding a rising 50-DMA at 308.59 with RSI at 68.6 and relative strength at highs. What makes that extraordinary is the contrast: over the same window GOOGL fell to -16.3% off its high, MSFT to -27.5%, NVDA to -19.3%, and the semiconductor complex was destroyed — AMAT -39.6%, LRCX -41.8%, ALAB -48.3%. The market spent this period repricing the cost side of the AI trade, and Apple, which spends comparatively little on AI infrastructure while collecting the consumer-monetisation side, became the rotation's beneficiary rather than its victim. The stock's VCP pattern remained intact through the entire drawdown in its peers.

The multiple is defensible while Services compounds and the buyback runs, but it prices in success, which is precisely why the 2-day earnings window argues for patience rather than aggression.

analyses.name: Eli Lilly and Company
analyses.verdict: Revenue +55.5% and EPS +169.9% at a $1.08T market cap, with RSI reset to 48.6 after a 42% quarter — the best structure in the entire 524-name scan.

financials.summary: Lilly's last full fiscal year was one of the most dramatic revenue expansions ever recorded by a company of its size. The incretin franchise — tirzepatide across both its diabetes and obesity indications — moved from launch phase into full commercial scale, and because the incremental gross margin on these products is very high, operating leverage was extreme: revenue grew rapidly and earnings grew several times faster. The scan captures the magnitude precisely: revenue +55.5% with EPS +169.9%. The counterweight in the accounts was capital intensity. Lilly spent aggressively on manufacturing capacity — new and expanded API and fill-finish plants — because supply, not demand, was the binding constraint on the franchise. That capex depressed free cash flow relative to earnings during the year, which is the correct trade to make when you are supply-constrained in a market this large. R&D also stepped up materially to defend the franchise across next-generation oral and combination candidates.
highlights: Revenue +55.5% YoY — extraordinary for a company of over $1 trillion in market value
EPS +169.9% YoY: incremental gross margin on the incretin franchise drove operating leverage roughly three times the revenue growth rate
Incretin franchise scaled from launch to become the primary revenue engine across both diabetes and obesity indications
Manufacturing capex stepped up sharply to relieve supply constraints — the main reason free cash flow lagged reported earnings
R&D spend increased to fund next-generation oral and combination incretin candidates
Forward P/E 26.9 — a modest multiple against a 55% revenue growth rate

accomplishments: Converted the incretin platform from a supply-constrained launch into a franchise generating majority-share revenue growth at trillion-dollar scale
Brought major new manufacturing capacity online, directly addressing the supply bottleneck that had been capping revenue
Achieved EPS growth roughly triple revenue growth, demonstrating the franchise's operating leverage rather than merely its demand
Built a next-generation pipeline — oral incretins and combination candidates — designed to extend the franchise past the current molecules' exclusivity
Crossed the $1 trillion market-capitalisation threshold, a first for the pharmaceutical sector

journey_52w.summary: A powerful advance followed by a healthy, complete reset. LLY closed this session at 1210.67, only 2.0% below its 52-week high, after gaining 42.5% over the prior three months. What makes the setup unusual is the RSI: 48.6. A stock does not normally sit at a neutral RSI two percent from an all-time high — that combination means the advance was followed by a genuine consolidation rather than a top. Volume dried to 0.67x through the pause, the VCP pattern qualified, relative strength stayed at highs, and the 50-DMA rose to 1141.45 beneath it. Through the same window the market's AI leadership was being liquidated, and Lilly's growth — which depends on prescriptions rather than data-centre budgets — was repriced as the more durable kind.

analyses.name: Datadog, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The one AI-adjacent name that kept its structure through the unwind: +97.2% in three months, RSI reset to 47.1, and TradingView's near-unanimous STRONG BUY at 17 buy / 1 sell.

financials.summary: Datadog's last full fiscal year was a consumption-growth story with an unusually clean profit inflection. Revenue grew +32.2% as observability spend expanded on two fronts: existing customers instrumenting more services (the land-and-expand mechanic that shows up as net revenue retention above 100%), and a new tranche of AI-native customers whose inference and training workloads generate large volumes of logs, metrics and traces. Crucially, EPS grew +104% — roughly triple the revenue rate — because the platform's gross margin is high and the sales-and-marketing ratio finally began to fall as a share of revenue. That is the transition from growth-at-any-cost to genuine operating leverage. Free cash flow conversion is strong for a company at this growth rate, and the balance sheet carries no meaningful stress. The caveat visible in the accounts is customer concentration in the AI-native cohort, whose consumption is more volatile than traditional enterprise spend.
highlights: Revenue +32.2% YoY on land-and-expand consumption growth plus a new AI-native customer cohort
EPS +104% YoY — roughly triple the revenue growth rate, marking a genuine operating-leverage inflection
High platform gross margin with sales-and-marketing declining as a percentage of revenue
Net revenue retention above 100%, meaning existing customers alone grow the revenue base
Strong free-cash-flow conversion relative to peers at comparable growth rates
Forward P/E 91.5 — the growth is real, but it is fully priced

accomplishments: Crossed from growth-stage spending into demonstrated operating leverage, with earnings compounding at triple the revenue rate
Captured the AI-native workload cohort, converting the AI buildout into observability consumption without taking on any capex exposure
Broadened from infrastructure monitoring into a multi-product platform spanning logs, APM, security and now AI/LLM observability — the driver of net revenue retention
Maintained net revenue retention above 100% through a period when enterprise software budgets were broadly scrutinised
Held a 52-week-high-adjacent structure through the July 2026 AI unwind, while comparable AI-levered names fell 40-55% off their highs

journey_52w.summary: A near-double followed by the deepest and cleanest reset of any winner in the scan. DDOG closed at 264.20, just 4.8% below its 52-week high, after +97.2% over three months — and with RSI at 47.1. That is a fully neutralised oscillator within five percent of a high, which is the technical signature of accumulation rather than exhaustion. Volume expanded to 1.58x through the base and the VCP pattern qualified above a 50-DMA at 242.62. The context is what matters most: this session saw semiconductor and data-centre infrastructure names liquidated — ALAB -48.3% off its high with RSI 12.3, VRT -40.7% with RSI 13.6, AMD -26.1%, AMAT -39.6% — and the market drew a sharp line between companies that spend on AI and companies that get paid when AI runs. Datadog sits firmly on the paid side, and its chart says so.

analyses.name: DaVita Inc.
analyses.verdict: Closed exactly at its 52-week high after +58.5% in three months with RSI only 66 — non-discretionary healthcare demand, and TradingView agrees at STRONG BUY 16/1.

financials.summary: DaVita's last full fiscal year was a margin-recovery year. Revenue grew a modest +6.0% — dialysis treatment volumes grow slowly and predictably, driven by demographics rather than by any commercial cycle — but EPS grew +43.5%, and that gap is the entire story. The recovery came from three places: commercial-payer mix and rate improvements that lifted revenue per treatment; labour cost normalisation after several years of clinical staffing inflation and agency-nurse premiums; and continued share repurchase, which DaVita funds with its consistently strong operating cash flow. The business carries meaningful financial leverage, which amplifies equity returns when margins expand — as they did — and would amplify them downward if reimbursement compressed. Cash generation is highly predictable because treatment volumes are medically necessary and largely non-deferrable.
highlights: EPS +43.5% YoY on revenue of only +6.0% — a pure margin-expansion year
Revenue per treatment improved on commercial-payer mix and rate negotiation
Clinical labour costs normalised after several years of staffing inflation, the single largest driver of the margin recovery
Strong and predictable operating cash flow funding a sustained buyback that amplifies per-share results
Meaningful balance-sheet leverage — the amplifier that made a 6% revenue year into a 43% earnings year
Forward P/E 14.0 despite +58.5% three-month price momentum

accomplishments: Restored margins to pre-inflation levels by working through the clinical staffing cost shock rather than by cutting capacity
Delivered EPS growth roughly seven times its revenue growth rate through mix, cost and buyback
Improved commercial payer mix and revenue per treatment in a reimbursement environment that is structurally difficult
Maintained treatment volume growth in line with the demographic trend, holding market position
Reached a 52-week high in July 2026 as capital rotated toward non-discretionary healthcare — one of very few names to close the session at a new high

journey_52w.summary: A quiet compounder that became a rotation destination. DVA closed this session at 240.98, precisely at its 52-week high, after +58.5% over three months — and it did so with RSI at 66.2 and volume at 0.85x, meaning the advance was orderly rather than climactic. The VCP pattern qualified, relative strength sat at highs, and the 50-DMA rose to 215.17 beneath it. The 58% move was not driven by any change in the business — dialysis volumes do not move 58% — but by a repricing of what non-cyclical, AI-uncorrelated cash flow is worth. As the market spent this period discovering that AI infrastructure earnings were not as visible as assumed, businesses whose demand is medically mandated were bid up. DaVita is close to the purest expression of that trade in the scan.

analyses.name: Liquidia Corporation
analyses.verdict: +127.6% in three months with RSI still only 55.9 and volume drying to 0.77x into the highs — the highest-momentum name in the scan that is somehow not overbought.

financials.summary: Liquidia's last full fiscal year was the transition from development-stage to commercial-stage, and the financial statements read accordingly. Revenue growth of +4,158% is arithmetically dramatic but should be read for what it is: the first full year of meaningful product revenue against a near-zero prior-year base, as the company's inhaled treprostinil therapy for pulmonary arterial hypertension and PH-ILD moved into commercial launch. The income statement still shows no positive EPS — commercial infrastructure, sales force build-out and ongoing clinical spend consume more than the gross profit on early-launch volumes, which is normal and expected at this stage. What matters analytically is not the loss but the trajectory of two lines: the revenue ramp rate quarter over quarter, and the cash runway. A single-product commercial-stage biotech is essentially a bet that the script ramp outpaces the cash burn, and the forward P/E of 14.9 in the scan implies the market is already modelling that crossover into profitability.

Transitioned from development-stage to commercial-stage across the fiscal year

accomplishments: Completed the transition from clinical-stage to commercial-stage, the single hardest step in biotech
Built and deployed a commercial organisation capable of driving a genuine script ramp in a specialist prescriber market

Delivered a share-price advance of +127.6% over three months while the broad market fell below its 50-DMA

journey_52w.summary: The scan's outlier: a stock that more than doubled in a quarter and still is not overbought. LQDA closed at 86.82, only 2.5% below its 52-week high, after +127.6% over three months — with RSI at 55.9 and volume contracted to 0.77x. Those numbers do not normally coexist. What they describe is an advance that came in distinct legs separated by tight, low-volume consolidations, rather than in one vertical move, which is why the VCP pattern qualified and relative strength sat at highs while the oscillator stayed mid-range. The 50-DMA rose steeply to 72.17 beneath the price. Over the same window the market was punishing speculative growth almost everywhere — quantum and space names in this scan sit 60-77% off their highs — so LQDA's advance was driven by company-specific commercial execution rather than by any risk-appetite tailwind. It had none.

analyses.name: Assurant, Inc.
analyses.verdict: The cleanest A+ setup on the board: -0.7% off the high with RSI at just 53.3, EPS +91.2%, forward P/E 12.5, and TradingView STRONG_BUY at 15/1.

financials.summary: Assurant's last full fiscal year was a strong underwriting and fee-income year across both of its main franchises — global lifestyle (mobile device protection, extended warranty, vehicle protection) and global housing (lender-placed and renters insurance). Revenue grew +11.3% while EPS grew +91.2%, and that gap has three sources. First, underwriting margins improved as earned pricing caught up with the loss-cost inflation of prior years — the same cycle benefiting the broader property-and-casualty complex. Second, net investment income rose materially because the float is reinvested at higher prevailing rates, which is close to pure margin. Third, Assurant runs a consistent buyback that concentrates the improved earnings into fewer shares. The mix is worth noting for quality: a substantial share of Assurant's revenue is fee-based service and administration income rather than pure underwriting risk, which makes results less catastrophe-sensitive than a typical P&C carrier.
highlights: EPS +91.2% YoY on revenue of +11.3% — margin expansion, not volume, drove the year
Underwriting margins improved as earned pricing caught up with prior-period loss-cost inflation
Net investment income rose on float reinvested at higher prevailing rates — close to pure incremental margin
Meaningful proportion of revenue is fee-based service and administration income, reducing catastrophe sensitivity versus a pure P&C carrier
Consistent share repurchase concentrated the earnings improvement into fewer shares
Forward P/E 12.5 — a low multiple for a business with a 91% earnings-growth year

accomplishments: Delivered EPS growth roughly eight times its revenue growth rate, demonstrating that the pricing cycle had fully caught up with loss costs
Grew the global lifestyle franchise — mobile device protection and extended warranty — which supplies recurring, fee-based, low-catastrophe-exposure revenue
Converted a higher interest-rate environment into materially higher net investment income on the float
Reached within 0.7% of its 52-week high in July 2026 while the S&P 500 closed the session below its 50-DMA
Earned the highest setup grade in the scan — an A+ VCP with RSI at 53.3, a combination almost no other top-20 name achieved

journey_52w.summary: A methodical, low-drama advance that ended in the tightest base in the scan. AIZ closed at 280.96, 0.7% below its 52-week high, after +21.2% over three months — with RSI at 53.3 and volume contracted to 0.85x. That RSI reading is the point: a stock within one percent of an all-time high with a mid-range oscillator has, by definition, consolidated rather than spiked, and the scan's VCP algorithm qualified the pattern accordingly. Relative strength sat at highs and the 50-DMA rose to 265.02 beneath. The macro context did the rest of the work: specialty insurance is precisely where capital went as the AI-capex trade unwound, because the earnings are driven by pricing cycles and investment yields rather than by data-centre budgets. Assurant offered that exposure with a fee-income buffer against catastrophe risk, which is a better version of the trade than a pure carrier.

analyses.name: Terreno Realty Corporation
analyses.verdict: Highest combined score in a 524-name universe (94.8): infill industrial REIT, -4.4% off the high, volume dried to 0.56x on the pullback — textbook accumulation.

financials.summary: Terreno's last full fiscal year was a strong one for a REIT of its type. Revenue grew +12.7% and reported EPS grew +40.2%, with the gap driven by two things: releasing spreads and asset sales. Terreno's model is narrow and deliberate — it owns infill industrial and logistics property in six coastal US markets where new supply is structurally constrained by land scarcity and zoning. That constraint is the entire investment case: when leases roll, they roll to substantially higher market rents, and the cash-rent spread on renewals is the primary driver of same-store growth. Occupancy remained high through the year. It is important to read the reported EPS carefully for any REIT — GAAP earnings include depreciation and gains on property dispositions, so they are a poor proxy for cash earnings; FFO and AFFO per share are the operative metrics, and the forward P/E of 41.2 in the scan reflects that GAAP distortion rather than a genuine 41x cash multiple. Leverage is conservative relative to the REIT peer group.

The macro backdrop through the period was two-sided for REITs: the rotation out of AI capex pushed capital toward real assets and yield, which helped, while the direction of the 10-year Treasury remained the governing variable. The Fed's decision to hold rates steady in this session removes near-term upside pressure on yields, which is the more supportive of the two possible outcomes.

analyses.name: CVS Health Corporation
analyses.verdict: EPS +63.1% at a forward P/E of 12.6 — the managed-care turnaround is landing while the stock still trades at a discount to the market.

financials.summary: CVS's last full fiscal year was the year the turnaround became visible in the numbers. Revenue grew +6.1% — steady, driven by pharmacy volumes, specialty drug growth and Aetna membership — while EPS grew +63.1%, and that gap is almost entirely about the medical loss ratio. The prior period had been defined by medical cost trend, particularly in Medicare Advantage, running well ahead of the rates CVS had priced. Over FY2025 the company repriced plans, exited unprofitable geographies and benefit designs, and let the pricing catch up to utilisation. The result was margin recovery in Health Care Benefits. Meanwhile the Health Services segment — pharmacy benefit management and specialty pharmacy — continued to generate the bulk of the cash flow, and the retail pharmacy footprint was rationalised. The business remains a three-part conglomerate with a substantial debt load, so the equity is levered to the margin recovery in both directions.

CVS closed at 105.92, 3.6% below its 52-week high, after +27.0% over three months, with RSI at 60.1 and volume contracted to 0.72x. The path here was not a growth story but a repair story: the market spent the prior period discounting the medical-cost-trend problem, and as each quarter showed the repricing working, the multiple recovered from distressed toward merely cheap. The July 2026 backdrop then added a second tailwind — as the AI trade unwound, capital sought businesses whose earnings did not depend on data-centre budgets, and a 12.6x forward multiple in defensive healthcare was an obvious destination. Notably, a managed-care cost datapoint landed in this session's newsflow via the Humana print, which held its outlook with medical costs in line — a modest positive read-through for the sector's cost trend.

analyses.name: Bank of America Corporation
analyses.verdict: Forward P/E 11.6, revenue +21.4%, EPS +36% — and 77 days to earnings, the cleanest event calendar of any top pick on the list.

financials.summary: Bank of America's last full fiscal year benefited from the two things that matter most to a money-centre bank: a favourable rate environment and a recovering capital-markets business. Revenue grew +21.4%, driven by net interest income expanding as the asset book repriced at higher yields faster than deposit costs rose, plus a genuine recovery in investment banking and trading revenue. EPS grew +36%, ahead of revenue, on operating discipline and a substantial buyback that has been steadily reducing share count. Credit quality remained benign through the year — charge-offs and provisions stayed within normalised ranges, and reserve builds were modest. Capital ratios remained comfortably above regulatory requirements, which is what allows the buyback to continue. The structural point about BAC specifically is its very large, low-cost deposit base, which is the source of its net interest margin advantage and also the reason it is more rate-sensitive than peers in both directions.

journey_52w.summary: A steady re-rating on the strength of the earnings, capped by the rotation. BAC closed at 61.07, 2.5% off its 52-week high, after +16.1% over three months, with RSI at 61.0 and volume at 0.92x. The VCP qualified, relative strength sat at highs, and the 50-DMA rose to 56.73 beneath. Two macro developments in this session shaped the setup directly. First, the Fed held rates steady — the most favourable outcome for a bank whose net interest margin depends on the current rate structure persisting, since cuts would compress it and hikes would strain credit. Second, capital continued rotating out of AI infrastructure into financials, where earnings are driven by rate spreads and credit rather than by data-centre capex. The result is a large-cap bank at 11.6x forward earnings with relative strength at highs and — the detail that matters most for a trade — no earnings print for 77 days.

analyses.name: NetApp, Inc.
analyses.verdict: +59.9% in three months at a forward P/E of 17.6 with 36 days to earnings — AI data-pipeline exposure without semiconductor cyclicality, and TradingView STRONG_BUY 15/1.

financials.summary: NetApp's last full fiscal year was a margin-and-mix year layered on top of a genuine AI-adjacent demand tailwind. Revenue grew +12.5% and EPS grew +23.4%, with the gap coming from product mix — all-flash storage arrays carry higher gross margin than the legacy hybrid systems they replace — and from continued growth in the public-cloud storage services business, which is subscription-like and higher margin than hardware. The demand driver worth understanding is that AI workloads are extremely data-hungry: training and inference pipelines require high-throughput, low-latency storage sitting next to the compute, and enterprises building internal AI capability have to solve the data layer regardless of which accelerator vendor they choose. That makes NetApp a beneficiary of AI adoption without exposure to the semiconductor capital cycle. Operating cash flow remained solid and the company continued returning capital through buybacks and dividends.

journey_52w.summary: The clearest illustration in the scan of the market's new distinction between AI spenders and AI beneficiaries. NTAP closed at 173.23, only 4.0% below its 52-week high, after +59.9% over three months, with RSI at 51.7, volume at 1.34x, and relative strength at highs above a 50-DMA at 158.90. Set that against the semiconductor names in the same universe on the same day: AMAT closed -39.6% off its high with RSI 25.9, LRCX -41.8% with RSI 19.4, ALAB -48.3% with RSI 12.3, AMD -26.1%. Both groups sell into the AI buildout, but semis sell into the capex line — which the market is now doubting — while storage sells into the data layer that has to be solved whether or not the next accelerator order is placed. NTAP's structure held, its multiple stayed modest at 17.6x, and it goes into the next session with 36 days before its own earnings, the widest event window of any technology name on my pick list.
